appraisal_events.evidence: il n'est pas ici pour être tourmenté... je ne veux pas qu'on le tourmente, moi !
appraisal_events.explanation: Mme Verdurin frames the pianist as someone whose comfort deserves protection rather than a performer to be commanded on demand, marking him as favored within the salon.

status_effects.explanation: Being shielded from being pressed into performing by the hostess marks him as a protected, valued member of the intimate circle rather than a mere instrument.

ambiguities: Swann's inclusion as 'entre camarades' and M. Verdurin's aside to him about the sonata are too thin and conventional (mere scene-setting courtesy) to constitute a distinct local status shift, so Swann was left unscored despite being mentioned.

The protective statement toward the pianist is the same utterance underlying the accepted snub of M. Verdurin; whether it constitutes a genuinely separate, non-redundant status effect for the pianist versus simply being folded into that already-captured dynamic is not fully certain.
